content.title: Why Are Stacks Important?
content.description: Stacks are one of the most widely used data structures in computer science. Many software systems rely on stack behavior to efficiently manage operations and data.

content.content: Although stacks appear simple, they power numerous real-world applications behind the scenes. Every time you navigate back in a browser, undo a change in a document, or call a function in a program, a stack is involved.

content.title: Interesting Fact
content.content: Every running program on your computer uses a stack internally to manage function calls and execution flow.
Overview of Stack Applications
Application 1: Function Call Stack
Every programming language uses a call stack to keep track of active function executions. Whenever a function is called, a new stack frame is pushed onto the call stack.

content.title: Stack Frame
content.description: A stack frame stores local variables, parameters, return addresses, and execution information for a function.

content.title: Real-World Usage
content.content: Java, Python, C++, JavaScript, and almost every programming language rely on call stacks.
Application 2: Recursion
Recursion works because function calls are stored in a stack. Every recursive call creates a new stack frame until the base condition is reached.

content.title: Stack Overflow
content.content: Too many recursive calls can exceed stack memory and cause a Stack Overflow error.
Application 3: Parentheses Matching
Stacks are commonly used to verify whether brackets, braces, and parentheses are balanced.

content.title: Core Idea
content.description: Opening brackets are pushed, and matching closing brackets pop them from the stack.

content.title: Compiler Usage
content.content: Compilers use this technique to validate source code syntax.
Application 4: Expression Evaluation
Stacks help evaluate mathematical expressions such as postfix, prefix, and infix expressions efficiently.
Application 5: Browser History
Web browsers use stacks to implement Back and Forward navigation functionality.

content.title: Implementation
content.description: Two stacks are commonly used: one for Back history and another for Forward history.

content.content: Application 6: Undo and Redo Operations
Editors and design tools maintain stacks to support undo and redo functionality.

content.title: Software Examples
content.content: Microsoft Word, VS Code, Photoshop, Figma, and many IDEs use stacks for Undo/Redo.
Application 7: Depth First Search (DFS)
Stacks play a critical role in graph traversal algorithms, especially Depth First Search.
Application 8: Compiler Design
Compilers use stacks extensively for parsing, syntax checking, expression conversion, and code generation.
Application 9: Backtracking Algorithms
Backtracking problems often use stacks explicitly or implicitly through recursion.

content.title: Common Problems
content.content: N-Queens, Sudoku Solver, Maze Solver, and Permutation Generation rely on stack-like behavior.
Application 10: Monotonic Stack Problems
Monotonic stacks help solve optimization problems efficiently by maintaining increasing or decreasing order.
Application Comparison
When Should You Think About Using a Stack?

content.title: Interview Tip
content.content: Whenever a problem involves nested structures, matching symbols, recursion, or nearest greater/smaller elements, consider using a Stack.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Many medium and hard interview questions become significantly easier once you identify the hidden stack pattern.
